source: ThermoML entry je049816w from versioned NIST 2020-09-30 archive SHA256 231161b5e443dc1ae0e5da8429d86a88474cb722016e5b790817bb31c58d7ec2. XML 8b9bb0d793b59d468c75800fc9fcc82f92c3452997c56d973749f47c2bf52ae7. Three row-matched pressure and independently chromatographed gas compositions, pairs(2,3),(4,5),(8,9), with 21,19,26 rows. ThermoML XML was decoded as a document for calibration; outcome NumValues for gas mole fraction and separately reported azeotrope values were never extracted. Evaporator temperature and liquid fractions, pure-acetal calibration, all mixture pressures and their expanded uncertainty were available to every fit. The numerical summary errors in the original paper Table6 and reported comparator coefficients were exposed as historical prior; no individual interior chromatographic outcome was used in designing or fitting any arm. The paper describes Wilson/NRTL pressure-only objective, SRK vapor and Poynting corrections.
hypothesis: One stable binary liquid mixing Gibbs energy per nominal isotherm, negligible composition-dependent liquid pressure contribution and ideal vapor for the tangent inverse; a finite convex potential may have kinks. Under this class each equilibrium vapor fraction defines an active line. Candidate is the midpoint of the numerically conservative projection interval at each liquid composition; not necessarily a jointly feasible path. The inner finite grid uses x as reported, ordered y at multiples of 1/256, pressure intervals with exact union propagation and backtraces two complete pressure/y witnesses. For continuous y use 256 cells with shared latent log pressure propagated through merged unions; one cell bin can relax the identity of y and x inside its boundaries. Continuous-box result is a numerical relaxation with a 2e-12 log guard, not formally interval-library certified. Fixed treated experimental pure limits, no outcome-derived endpoints. For both sets each true mixture pressure at the isotherm midpoint can vary within the published per-row NIST expanded pressure range after an additional conditional |d log P/dT|<=.06 K^-1 allowance, an engineering assumption distinct from measured mixture temperature slopes. The outer box additionally takes nominal x ±.005 within [0,1] for every interior row; x endpoints fixed. Only numerical bounds conditional on these assumptions, no probability coverage or fully identified smooth potential.
curvature: Take the measured pressure maximum. For an interior maximum use symmetric stride1 and2 nonuniform three-point second differences of log pressure at the reported liquid composition. Propagate individual pressure endpoints and same temperature allowance, keep signs and both strides. No alternate smoothing, selecting another maximum or claiming exact derivative without a third/fourth derivative remainder. Composition and finite-grid bias mean these conditional secants do not themselves measure the thermodynamic curvature of a true azeotrope. For endpoint maxima no local interior test. The relation (vV−vL)P″/gV_yy=s(s−1) applies to smooth, stable, two-phase coexistence, fixed T, positive vapor curvature and positive phase-volume gap at y=x; complementary positive s can share local curvature.
controls: Six pressure-side point controls: ideal liquid/Raoult with SRK vapor, actual original DDBST UNIFAC group assignment and package version0, original Table6 Wilson and NRTL coefficients with Table5 constants, and separate relative-pressure-squared refits of Wilson and NRTL (alpha=.4) using all available pressure/liquid composition/row temperature observations only. Vapor uses Soave-Redlich-Kwong quadratic attractive/linear covolume, zero cross interaction coefficient assumed as no value specified; fixed source volumes at 298.15K for Poynting. Published-parameter reproductions are not archived row-by-row author forecasts. Original UNIFAC uses thermo0.6.0. All pressure/source calibration differences and possible finite temperature range violations reported. Accuracy comparison requires beating all six; same input data permitted to each arm, physical feature models use different assumptions.
outcomes: All 66 gas-fraction assay rows retained; primary tests use every one of 60 interior rows (19/17/24), six pure endpoints separate deterministic controls with no interior-score credit. Per isotherm four gates: at least90% observed central assay values inside outer box intervals; median full width <= .05 mole fraction (10 times the quoted composition accuracy); lower interior mean absolute error AND lower worst absolute error than every point control, strict. All 12 gates compulsory. Width/calibration are predeclared decision criteria, not measurement guarantees. Most extreme absolute interior midpoint error pooled, measured row, source pressure, all point arms and intervals retained. If nominal inner discrete graph empty, retain as such; it cannot prove continuous infeasibility. If outer relaxation has no full path refuse to forecast; no postmeasurement width, tail, grade or model changes.
